correctness.rationale: The partial derivatives, divided by twice the respective nonzero coordinate, give the principal subsystem on coordinate squares for the symmetric matrix with diagonal 2 and off-diagonal r,s,s. Two-coordinate singularities give r or s = ±2; in the remaining case the determinant is 2(2-r)(r+2-s²) and at s²=r+2 the all-nonzero kernel vector is (1,1,-s). Genus is three. In the standard quartic Hasse–Witt coefficient rule all off-diagonals have an odd exponent and vanish. Independent truncated polynomial multiplication gives exactly the diagonal entries A,A,B and the asserted identities. Diagonality preserves support under every Frobenius twist, so the stable rank is 2[A≠0]+[B≠0], and rank-zero Cartier in genus three is equivalent to superspeciality. Removing r=2 leaves the three reduced A factors (the two linear-in-r factors are primitive, their coefficient and constant having no common root); each of the five distinct B factors is a graph in s. Same-group crossings occur only on the excluded boundary. Restricting each L_i to a B graph in t=s² gives the two roots 4 and the stated retained t_i; the first is excluded and the second is simple and nonzero in each case. Thus the scheme of A=B=0 is reduced by the nonzero derivative after t=s² or the independent gradients at s=0. For c=0,±5 the L2 arguments are 1,5,9 (all squares over F11), and their L1 multiples by 8 are nonsquares there. For c=±ω the two norms are 9,1, hence both arguments are squares over F121. The independent branch census over F11 and F121 via θ²=2 verified smoothness counts, all branch multiplicities of the retained meetings and rank frequencies (9,14,18,32), (25,326,560,13132). Enumeration supports the finite counts, not the algebraic-closure proof. The supplied script was inspected, not executed.
